dataset: CommonsenseQA (tau/commonsense_qa, train+validation; test has no gold), HellaSwag (Rowan/hellaswag, train+validation; test has no gold) and MMLU (cais/mmlu config 'all', test+validation+dev; auxiliary_train excluded as a mix of other datasets), read from the HuggingFace auto-converted parquet via the datasets-server parquet API. For each multiple-choice question this audit measures, per benchmark, how the length of the gold option compares with its distractors -- by characters (after stripping) and by whitespace tokens -- reporting how often the gold is the unique longest / unique shortest option, the accuracy of a tie-aware 'pick the longest' heuristic versus the random-choice baseline, and the mean gold vs distractor length. It tests whether audit 51's crowd-authored-vs-exam-sourced length-shortcut split generalizes. Measures a construction property of the benchmark, not model output.
note: P1 (structural, finding either way): every benchmark parses with 0 bad_key and 0 degenerate questions over its gold-bearing splits. P2 (directional headline, finding either way): audit 51's split generalizes -- the gold is the UNIQUE longest option more often than the random-choice baseline in BOTH crowd-authored benchmarks (CommonsenseQA, HellaSwag) AND at or below chance in exam-sourced MMLU. P3 (exploitability, finding either way): in each crowd-authored benchmark a tie-aware 'pick the longest' heuristic beats the random-choice baseline. 'longest_accuracy' is the expected accuracy of a heuristic that always picks the longest option and splits ties uniformly. Lengths are characters after str.strip(); a token view is reported alongside. Measures AGREEMENT with a length heuristic, not correctness of any model.
